topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and establishes its objectives before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Biological origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through clonal evolution and the sources of mutations that contribute to it.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and their interpretation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for environmental contributions to cancer risk and how that evidence is interpreted.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents contribute to cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a specific example.

topics.label: Carcinogen activation and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how carcinogenic exposures produce DNA damage through mechanisms shaped by activation and repair.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tissue conditions shape the progression from carcinogenic exposure to tumour development and conclude with a summary of those mechanisms.

topics.label: Human evidence of carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how measurable evidence in humans supports the identification of carcinogen exposure and assessment of carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate experimental tests used to identify carcinogenic hazards and the limitations of their results.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk–benefit conclusions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by drawing together its findings on environmental cancer risks and carcinogenicity assessment.
